meta.title: Motion
meta.description: Which movements are animated, and how the schedule answers a reader who asked for less of it.

basics.intro: Two things move: a jump between shifts scrolls smoothly, and a pinned chip slides in rather than appearing. Both are off when the reader has asked for reduced motion, and both are off when you turn the animation flag off.
points: reducedMotion is 'auto' by default and follows the system’s prefers-reduced-motion.
Under reduced motion every CSS transition in the component is removed, not shortened — a jump lands at once, and nothing fades.
enableAnimations turns the motion off regardless of the system setting, for a page that is deliberately still.
Scrolling by hand is never affected: that is the browser’s, not the component’s.
Reduced motion is honored without a setting of your own: the system preference is enough.
Nothing depends on an animation finishing. Every landing is correct at the moment it is asked for, and the smooth scroll is only how it gets there.
A jump moves focus to the shift heading whether it animates or not, so a keyboard reader lands in the same place either way.
enableAnimations removes the entrance animation of the pinned chips.
prefersReducedMotion from /dom gives the same reading to markup of your own.
The durations are fixed by the stylesheet; there is no prop for how long a transition lasts.
There is no animation between the two views — the switch is immediate by design.
Smooth scrolling depends on the browser honoring scroll-behavior; where it does not, the jump is simply instant.
